accounting.howToReadThese: Two dispatches happened before this one: one was refused before it could write anything and was ruled unspent, the other wrote its marker and is spent.  This attempt wrote its marker too, so it is spent as well.  Two production chances are gone in total, none is left, no boot has been started, and no image counts as produced.
accounting.note: The authority on disk still reads runsPerformed 0.  It is left byte-unchanged rather than corrected, exactly as the previous authority was: the marker is what spends an attempt, and the records that count them are these stop records.  The result document written beside this one reads runsPerformed 1.

producerFingerprintAfterTheAttempt.whyItIsNotReSealed: It is a record of the bytes that ran, taken before they ran.  Re-sealing it now would make it pin a file that never produced anything, which is the one thing it exists to rule out.  The four files that are the producer proper -- the module, the wrapper, the workflow and the frozen helper -- are byte-unchanged and still match.  The fifth is the gate file, and its drift is declared here rather than absorbed quietly.

repairsThatHeldNote: All three fixes the previous stop bought did their job.  The result document assembled without raising, the marker came off the runner and is byte-identical on both replicas, and the files a failed replica produced were kept under a name that disowns them.  There is something to look at this time because of them.
